text: This is a good water filter. We like that the filter clips onto the pitcher and stays there - it makes it easy to refill. Our only complaint, however, is that the filter cover does not stay on. Apart from this inconvenience, this is a good way to filter your water.

I am confused by the reviews here on Amazon for this product. Many seem to be reviewing a completely different product than the one I received.

I have the "leading brand" and have used it for years and while I love it, it is very slow. However, the filters are cheap and they work. I tried another brand that was great while it lasted, but it fastened its water feed to the faucet, so when I got a new integrated spray faucet, the unit became totally useless.

This is an interesting idea. It spreads out the filter like a drip coffee maker. This larger area makes the water pass through faster. It would be impossible for it to pass as slowly as my leading brand, and some people are saying it is slower, which based on physics is impossible.

Five times faster? Well, maybe not. And it still tries your patience a bit waiting at the faucet. Timing it accurately though, it filters the water about 3-4 times faster. Filter cost, however, may not be cost effective relative to the cheap filters I get in bulk for the "leading brand".

It is definitely faster. It is cosmetically much more appealing. It cleans easily. So it wins on all fronts....EXCEPT FILTER COST. The FILTERS ARE MUCH MUCH MORE EXPENSIVE at up to $10 a pop. I get my current filters in bulk for about $3. a pop for the "leading brand". I am not certain I would be willing to pay that kind of difference when it comes time to replace the filter which

This filter unfortunately does not seem to perform as advertised. While there is a lot to like about it, it only offers trade-offs over current filters on the market. Ultimately it's more of a hassle over traditional filters.

Setup and activation of the filter is a process. There are a number of components that need to be washed and assembled. The filter needs to be soaked for some time, and due to the fact that the filter tends to float, I spent the time to hold it under the water to ensure a complete activation. It never actually stayed submerged during this process. The final step is shaking the filter.

Once assembled, it performed nicely for a few days. I could leave the pitcher in the sink to fill up under a moderate stream and it would only take a minute or so. The performance quickly dropped, however. Now it takes a few minutes to fill up under only a trickle. Any faster and the reservoir on top overflows and leaks into the filtered water. It seems like a step backward.

The other filters on the market that have a more thorough filter and a larger reservoir actually perform better. You can fill up your water bottle from the pitcher, then fill up the pitcher reservoir walk away. With this, you have to stand there waiting for it to fill. It's a step backward. And the fact that the filter on this product is only a fraction of the filtering capability of others doesn't really help.
